name: AiSOC — one-click dev
//image: Prebuilt image is published by .github/workflows/devcontainer-build.yml. It drops Codespaces cold-start from ~5 min → ~30 s by baking Node + pnpm + Python (+ uv) + Go + Docker + gh into a single layer instead of resolving them via `features:` on every boot.
//build: Fallback for local devcontainer-cli use and for forks that don't have GHCR pull access. The `image` directive above wins; the build block is only consulted by tooling like `devcontainer build`.
//features: We intentionally do NOT enable docker-in-docker / python / go / github-cli features here — the *binaries* are baked into the image at build time and re-enabling the features would cancel the cold-start win. But see runArgs/mounts/postStartCommand below: the docker-in-docker feature also supplies container runtime options and a dockerd entrypoint, and that half has no Dockerfile equivalent. Omitting it is what broke the Codespaces quickstart (#716).
//runArgs: The half an image cannot provide. Capabilities are granted at container creation, so a Dockerfile cannot self-grant them: without --privileged the container ran with CapEff: 0 and CAP_SYS_ADMIN outside the bounding set, so not even sudo could start dockerd. --init reaps the zombies a background dockerd leaves behind.
//mounts: dockerd's overlay2 graph driver cannot run on the container's own overlay filesystem. A named volume gives it a real one, and keeps pulled images across a Codespace stop/resume so the demo does not re-pull on every boot.
//onCreateCommand: Runs once at image-spawn time. The pnpm store is already warm in the prebuilt image, so this is fast (<= 30 s on a green Codespace). `--frozen-lockfile` matches CI and the web image: a contributor's first install must produce the dependency set CI tested, or their first green run is a different build from everyone else's. It read `--frozen-lockfile=false`, which a substring test for the flag reads as enabling the very thing it disables.
//postStartCommand: Starts dockerd. Runs on every container start rather than only at create, so a Codespace stop/resume comes back with a working daemon — `onCreateCommand` would leave the second boot without one.
postAttachCommand:
echo '
>>> AiSOC dev container is ready.
>>> To run the demo, open a terminal and run:
>>>     pnpm aisoc:demo --no-open
>>> Then click the forwarded port 3000 in the Ports panel.
>>> Or, no-Docker:  pip install -e packages/aisoc-sandbox && aisoc-sandbox demo
'
